enquiry: We want to monitor water content in a clear ethanol-water stream in our solvent recovery unit. Water content is between 0.5 and 5 % w/w, the line runs at 25 °C in a DN50 stainless steel pipe, and the analyzer can sit in a control room about 20 m away. Our reference is Karl Fischer titration in the lab, and we need an updated value every minute.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with water content control in the solvent recovery unit, and what action would you take if you knew the water content every minute?
clarification_questions.why: Identifies the decision that real-time data drives and whether the goal is control, quality release or troubleshooting.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Goal is process monitoring of water content; the decision and its tolerance are unknown and will be established in the first conversation.

clarification_questions.question: What other components are present in the stream besides ethanol and water, and at what levels?
clarification_questions.why: Other absorbing or scattering species can interfere with the water measurement and determine the calibration matrix.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Stream is treated as ethanol-water only; any further components are unknown and must be checked in lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: How do temperature, flow, pressure and bubbles vary in the line, and is fouling or cleaning (CIP) applied to the pipe?
clarification_questions.why: Temperature, bubbles and fouling change the optical signal and determine probe type and maintenance.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Conditions are stable at the stated 25 °C with no bubbles or fouling; this must be confirmed in an in-line trial.

clarification_questions.question: Where on the DN50 line would the probe be installed, does a port or window exist there, and is contact with the liquid permitted?
clarification_questions.why: The installation point and contact allowance decide between a transmission, transflection or ATR-type probe.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point and contact are unknown; the probe choice stays open until the installation point is confirmed.

clarification_questions.question: Are there existing fibers, cables or analyzers between the line and the control room, and what is the actual cable route length?
clarification_questions.why: Fiber type and cable length determine which wavelengths reach the analyzer and whether a remote setup is possible.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: No existing fiber is assumed; the 20 m is the only distance stated and the fiber type is undecided.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, precision and sampling frequency does the Karl Fischer reference method achieve, and how many lab samples per day are taken?
clarification_questions.why: The reference accuracy sets what an online sensor must match and how the calibration will be validated.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference accuracy is unknown; the online method will be compared against the KF data in a lab screening step.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy and response time are required for the one-minute value across the 0.5 to 5 % w/w range, and what is the budget range?
clarification_questions.why: Accuracy, response time and budget decide whether a single-method sensor or a more complex system is justified.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Accuracy, response time and budget are unknown; the simplest method that meets the stated one-minute update will be proposed first.

flags_before_revision.detail: overstated: The claim says mid-IR 'needs chalcogenide or polycrystalline fibers'. S02 p.6 lists these as options but also lists hollow glass waveguides (2000 nm-18 um) and indium and zirconium fluoride fibers as covering mid-IR wavelengths, so the page does not show that these two fiber types are the only requirement. Fix: State that mid-IR transmission is covered by several fiber types on S02 p.6, including chalcogenide and polycrystalline fibers, and that no link length is given for them.

different_context: Fig. 8 on S01 p.18 is a multispectral laboratory setup for milk analysis, not an inline process example. The claim calls it the 'inline milk example' and transfers the lab-based statement about transmission to inline use without saying so. Fix: Describe the S01 p.18 example as a laboratory milk analysis setup, and attribute the inline monitoring point only to the page's general text about inline monitoring.

not_supported: None of the cited pages mention fouling control or a 20 m link. The cited table rows give optical path, sensitivity and cost ratings for IR, NIR, Raman, UV-Vis and fluorimetry methods, not fouling requirements for this application. Fix: Remove 'fouling control' or mark it as an unverified engineering consideration not supported by the cited pages.

not_supported: S02 p.6 does not state a 20 m link length. It only shows fiber transmission ranges. The claim that 'About 20 m stated' is therefore not supported by the cited page. Fix: Remove the statement that 20 m is stated, and say that no link length is given on S02 p.6.

not_supported: S01 p.10 covers ATR probes, NIR basics, overlapping bands and chemometrics. It does not say that unlisted stream components can invalidate a matrix-specific calibration. Fix: Cite a page that discusses matrix or calibration validity, or rephrase the risk as a general chemometrics consideration supported by S01 p.10 (overlapping absorption bands).

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
